_README: Deliberate Setlist removals, acknowledged so the health-check guard passes. One entry per ShowID. 'entries' are the exact strings removed; 'why' must say why they were not songs. Anything removed WITHOUT an entry here blocks the push.

38936833f4cd.why: Provenance lines from the header of the folder's info.txt, imported into Setlist as if they were songs. The real setlist is the disc's 18 numbered tracks, which the field now holds; two of those tracks were missing while this junk was present.

entries: Dave & Nate Inteview - The Monday Dump 2002
f05548617099.why: Header line, two menu/section labels and a bonus-feature title imported into Setlist as songs. The disc's bonus material and its second programme ('The Monday Dump') are described in Notes instead.

39543a8a44a5.why: Three header lines and a running time from the sidecar, plus 'Dave Talks' which the sidecar numbers as a track but is a spoken segment, not a song. Recorded in Notes. The rebuild ADDS 'Hey, Johnny Park!', which the record was missing.

8349e6f453e8.why: The band name, date and venue lines from the head of info.txt, imported as songs. The date and venue were moved into their own fields. The rebuild ADDS 'Hey, Johnny Park!', 'Alone + Easy Target' and a second 'Jam'.

2cc4ba6da8d1.why: Not a setlist. The three words are an English sentence fragment split on spaces - almost certainly a note such as "Didn't figure out" written into the field and later delimited. No setlist is known for this show.

entries: broadcast by Europe2 TV french cable/satellite channel
removed the TV logo with VirtualDub Mod using LogoAway filter
DVD inlay artwork by Pierre L
27726121cfae.why: Three header lines and eight lines of transfer/authoring notes from the sidecar, imported as songs. The venue and country were moved into their own fields; the broadcast source is recorded in Notes. All thirteen real songs are kept.

8ddd13481eb7.why: SPLIT BILL. Thirteen of these are GREEN DAY songs sitting in a Foo Fighters record, along with four header lines. Green Day play the first ~47 minutes; Foo Fighters' seven songs are kept. Green Day's set is not catalogued anywhere - this folder should be split into two records, and until it is, their songs are deliberately not listed under Foo Fighters.

entries: V. Tales of Another Broken Home
78ace4edbb43.why: Not removed - RETAINED inline. These are the five movements of the single 9:29 track 'Jesus of Suburbia', which the record had listed as five separate songs, making a nine-song set look like five. They now appear inside that one entry. The sidecar's 'VI. Dearly Beloved' is a typo for IV and is corrected.

0a9a2978c904.why: Two header lines from the sidecar plus an instruction line telling the reader where the screenshots are, all imported into Setlist as songs. The two real songs are Who covers, which is what VH1 Rock Honors 2008 was: a Who tribute.

6f96566d4bb9.why: The band name, sitting as the first entry of its own setlist - a header line from the sidecar. Nothing else was removed; 'Are You In?' was ADDED from the same sidecar.

ff25a03fa586.why: Five interview segments, not songs. The zdf.kultur broadcast interleaves them with the music and the sidecar numbers all seventeen items together; Setlist is songs only, and the interleaving is described in Notes. 'Are You In?' was ADDED from the same sidecar.

cc0a258b1e62.why: A disc title and a seeding note from METRO.txt, imported as if they were songs. Neither was ever a song. The disc is a compilation of four unrelated programmes, now described in Notes; no setlist is known for any of them.

entries: [MTV Video Music Awards, New York, Sep 8 1994]
2343bb4e36cb.why: Bracketed section headers, not songs. They separated the four shows this disc holds. The disc was split into four records on 2026-08-24, so each header is now a record's own date and venue fields, and the songs beneath each header moved to the record for that show: 3a96a7ccf97a (Astoria), bc823312e8f8 (Rock am Ring), 8aa0469c0797 (MTV VMAs). This record keeps the Barcelona songs.

afc33e08e173.why: The band name and the venue name from the head of info.txt, imported as songs. 'Geek U.S.A' is not a loss: it is respelled 'Geek U.S.A.' with the trailing period the sidecar actually uses. The rebuild also ADDS '(unknown instrumental)', which the sidecar lists between Siva and Silverfuck and the record was missing.

3cbf2c1669ea.why: The band name is a header line. The songs are real, but they belong to the 1993-09-23 Guildhall, Southampton show, which is NOT on this disc: the disc declares that titleset at 1:23:07 but it has no video files at all, only IFO and BUP. The only footage present is the Astoria 1994-02-24 segment, whose five songs the field now holds. The Southampton setlist is preserved in full in this record's Notes so nothing is lost if the footage is ever found.

67729ca10fe1.why: Three artist names, a description line and the uploader's handle, taken from the head and foot of sp_zwan_corgan_DVD1.txt. None was a song. The disc is eleven separate TV appearances kept as one record; each is named in Notes with its date where known.

entries: Tibetan Freedom Concert (MTV Week In Rock)
ed0287648e21.why: The event name from the head of the sidecar, imported as a song. It now lives in EventOrFestival. The rebuild ADDS 'Tonight, Tonight', which the sidecar lists between Zero and Fuck You and the record was missing.

entries: shot for a school project by a friend of the band
contains B&W footage from an unknown show at Metro in late 1989 or early 1990
different footage from the MTV News Report on the Double Door shows
songs not available on other versions of this show
thanks to Josh Provost and Matt Krueger for sending me their tapes to transfer
49a9bdb96d61.why: Descriptive prose and credits from tsp_90-03_comp.txt, imported as songs. The sidecar describes a 1990-2003 compilation of eight segments, but only ONE was ever downloaded - the folder holds a single titleset plus a uTorrent part file. That titleset is the sidecar's segment 04, Eurockeennes 1997-07-04, whose three songs the field now holds and whose 13:19 runtime matches the record exactly. 'Ava Adore' is a real song but belongs to segment 05 (TFI Friday 1998), which is not on the drive.

866724a0da11.why: This record was carrying the setlist of a DIFFERENT night. The list came from the sidecar of the 1998-04-23 disc (record 5795828263c1) and does not match this recording. This disc's own sidecar, tsp19980523.txt, gives a different eleven-item list and a running time of 1:23:40, which the field now holds. 'Once Upon A Time' and 'Bullet With Butterfly Wings' appear in both nights but are respelled here as this sidecar spells them. Nothing is lost: the April setlist remains on the April record.

entries: DO NOT ENCODE TO VCD OR SVCD (OR ANY LOSSY FORMAT) AND DO NOT SELL

31b63a1524eb.why: The whole of 'The Smashing Pumpkins - Holland 1994-1995.txt' had been pasted into Setlist: two header lines, an authoring note, a distribution warning and five paragraphs of the uploader's notes, none of them songs. The notes themselves are preserved in this record's Notes. The disc's second programme, the Loladamusica special, was split out to record cc936661297a on 2026-08-24 and its five songs moved there verbatim.

eef227d6df44.why: The band name from the head of 'SP - 1996-05-04_DVD.txt', imported as a song. The rebuild ADDS 'Tonight, Tonight', which the sidecar lists as the fifth track and the record was missing.

a48ff7a15905.why: The first two header lines of the folder's sidecar EXTRAS_TS/'2001-06-04 Landgraaf, NL (PAL).txt' - the artist name and the festival name - imported into Setlist as if they were songs. The 15 entries that remain match the sidecar's numbered 'Set:' block exactly.

5740c44ce4e4.why: Two header lines from the folder's info.txt imported as songs. The rebuild also ADDS '15 Step', the sidecar's track 3, which the record was missing, and marks the list incomplete on the sidecar's own statement that Radiohead played 23 tracks and the BBC broadcast 14.

81f30a948836.why: 'General' is the MediaInfo section header from the sidecar's technical dump, imported as a song. The rebuild ADDS '15 Step' and '2+2=5', the sidecar's tracks 3 and 4, which the record was missing.

entries: Packed like Sardines in a Crushd Tin Box
c7821268dcef.why: Not removals - spelling corrections to 'The National Anthem' and 'Packt Like Sardines in a Crushd Tin Box', the correct song titles and the forms already used on 493b8c833d73. The guard compares normalised strings, so a retitle reads as a loss. The setlist grows from 6 to the sidecar's 13.

entries: Packed like Sardines in a Crushd Tin Box
87b69f8144b4.why: Same spelling corrections as its sibling c7821268dcef, for the same reason.

3b82b5656ac2.why: The band name and the venue, taken from the first two lines of the folder's info.txt and imported into Setlist as if they were the opening two songs. The nine entries after them are the sidecar's own list and are unchanged; VenueName now holds 'Cabaret Metro' where it belongs.

4e10917e766c.why: Three lines from the head of the sidecar and two from its sign-off, imported as songs. The eleven real songs are the sidecar's own numbered list 01-11 and are unchanged. 'Length 59 minutes' also turned out to be true and correct the stored runtime, which was 1743s against a demuxed 3564s.

entries: I recorded this from the stands
but its the only recording of this show that i have come across
i have traded it a couple of times but its reasonably circulated
cb1798848f6d.why: Not one of these was ever a song. The whole field was the folder's BDO.txt pasted in wholesale - band name, festival name, the taper's warning that the disc menu is mis-dated, and his notes on the recording. The sidecar carries no setlist at all, so the replacement is setlist.fm's Big Day Out Sydney 2008 entry (78 attendee confirmations), 16 entries including the encore break. The same paste is why ShowDate was 2010-01-09, the torrent's upload timestamp.

entries: TV broadcast (proshot) from the Up promotional tour. I got this from murmurs tracker in June 2006 where it was seeded by Crazy
f421a2ba84cf.why: The Setlist field held no songs at all - it was the sidecar's opening sentence, the band name and its trailer line, split on semicolons. The same sidecar lists 18 numbered tracks, which the field now holds. Nothing was a song, so nothing is lost.
